classification.difficultyReason: Combine an initial lump sum with a geometric series of deposits, then solve for the initial amount.

content.prompt:
An investment account begins with an amount $P$.
A further $\$5000$ is deposited at the end of each year for 15 years.
The account earns 8% p.a., and its value at the end of 15 years is $\$180\,000$.
Write an expression for the final value in terms of $P$ and find the initial amount $P$. Give the monetary answer to the nearest cent.

answer.worked:
The starting amount grows for 15 years to $P(1.08)^{15}$.
At the end of 15 years, the regular deposits are worth
$$5000(1.08)^{14}+5000(1.08)^{13}+\cdots+5000.$$
The deposit terms form a geometric series with $a=5000$, common ratio $1.08$ and $n=15$.
$$\begin{align*}FV&=P(1.08)^{15}+\frac{5000(1.08^{15}-1)}{1.08-1}\\180000&=P(1.08)^{15}+\frac{5000(1.08^{15}-1)}{0.08}\\P(1.08)^{15}&=180000-\frac{5000(1.08^{15}-1)}{0.08}\\P&=\frac{180000-\frac{5000(1.08^{15}-1)}{0.08}}{1.08^{15}}\\P&\approx13946.11\end{align*}$$
The regular deposits are worth approximately $\$135\,760.57$, leaving approximately $\$44\,239.43$ attributable to the starting amount. The account must begin with $\$13\,946.11$.
